voices.name: Sam Altman
voices.bio: Sam Altman leads OpenAI, the organization behind GPT-4, GPT-4o, o1, and the ChatGPT platform used by hundreds of millions worldwide. Under his leadership OpenAI has produced some of the most capable AI systems ever built and accelerated the global AI race significantly.
known_for: Brief ouster and reinstatement as CEO in 2023
positions: AGI is coming sooner than most expect
AI will be the most transformative technology in human history
Safety and capability can be pursued simultaneously
voices.note: Vursyl covers Sam Altman's contributions to AI honestly. OpenAI was founded in 2015 as a nonprofit with a mission to develop AI for the benefit of humanity. Altman subsequently led its transformation into a capped-profit and now fully for-profit entity — a shift that drew criticism from co-founders including Elon Musk, who filed a lawsuit alleging the organization abandoned its founding mission. The nonprofit-to-for-profit conversion is ongoing as of 2026 and remains contested in California courts. These are documented facts, not editorializing.

voices.name: Dario Amodei
voices.bio: Dario Amodei co-founded Anthropic after leaving OpenAI as VP of Research. He leads the development of the Claude family of models and pioneered Constitutional AI — a method of training AI systems to be helpful, harmless, and honest without relying solely on human feedback.
positions: AI safety and frontier capability must advance together
Constitutional AI is a scalable path to aligned models
The next few years of LLM development are uniquely formative

voices.name: Andrej Karpathy
voices.bio: Andrej Karpathy co-founded OpenAI, led Tesla Autopilot as Director of AI, coined the term 'vibe coding,' and founded Eureka Labs before joining Anthropic's pre-training team in May 2026 to use Claude to accelerate the research that builds the next version of Claude. One of the most consequential AI practitioners alive.
known_for: Neural Networks: Zero to Hero YouTube series
positions: AI-assisted research loops will compress model development cycles
Education infrastructure for AI is critically underdeveloped
Pre-training remains the most important frontier in LLM research

voices.name: Demis Hassabis
voices.bio: Demis Hassabis co-founded DeepMind in 2010 and has led it through AlphaGo, AlphaFold, AlphaStar, and Gemini. He won the Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 2024 for AlphaFold's contribution to protein structure prediction. One of the most decorated scientist-entrepreneurs in history.
positions: AI will be the most powerful tool humanity has ever created for scientific discovery
Games are ideal training grounds for general intelligence
Safety must be built into AI systems from the ground up

voices.name: Yann LeCun
voices.bio: Turing Award winner and pioneer of convolutional neural networks — the architecture underlying most modern computer vision. Chief AI Scientist at Meta. Outspoken critic of the view that current LLMs are a path to AGI, and advocate for world models and autonomous machine intelligence.
positions: LLMs alone cannot achieve human-level intelligence
World models are essential for autonomous AI
Open-source AI is critical for safety and democratization

voices.name: Geoffrey Hinton
voices.bio: The 'Godfather of Deep Learning.' Nobel Prize winner in Physics 2024. His foundational work on backpropagation and neural networks in the 1980s laid the groundwork for every modern AI system. Left Google in 2023 to speak freely about AI risks. One of the most influential scientists of the 20th and 21st centuries.
positions: AI development may be moving faster than society can adapt
The field needs more focus on understanding what neural networks actually learn
Existential risk from AI is a legitimate concern worth taking seriously

voices.name: Fei-Fei Li
voices.bio: Creator of ImageNet — the dataset that sparked the deep learning revolution. Co-Director of Stanford's Human-Centered AI Institute. Former Chief Scientist of AI at Google Cloud. Champion of human-centered, equitable, and accessible AI development.
positions: AI must be developed with human values and needs at the center
Diversity in AI research produces better and safer outcomes
ImageNet-scale data curation is as important as model architecture

voices.name: Andrew Ng
voices.bio: AI educator to millions. Co-founded Google Brain and Coursera. Leads Landing AI applying AI to enterprise and manufacturing. His online courses have trained more practicing AI engineers than any institution on earth.
positions: AI is the new electricity — infrastructure for every industry
AI education at scale is the highest-leverage investment in the field
Practical AI deployment matters more than theoretical benchmarks

voices.name: Ilya Sutskever
voices.bio: Co-founder of OpenAI and its former Chief Scientist. Led research through GPT-2, GPT-3, GPT-4, and DALL-E. Founded Safe Superintelligence Inc. (SSI) in 2024 with a singular focus: building safe superintelligent AI with no product distractions.
known_for: Central role in the 2023 OpenAI board drama
positions: Superintelligence safety must be solved before superintelligence is built
The current generation of models may be more capable than we understand
Research focus should be undiluted by product pressures

voices.name: Elon Musk
voices.bio: Leads xAI (Grok LLM), SpaceX (Starship, Starlink), and Tesla (Optimus humanoid, FSD). Co-founded OpenAI in 2015 before departing and later filing suit against it. Commands the largest combined AI, space, and robotics portfolio of any individual on earth.
positions: Open-source AI is essential to prevent dangerous concentration of power
SpaceX making humanity multiplanetary is the most important long-term project
Humanoid robots will transform the physical economy
voices.note: Elon Musk co-founded OpenAI in 2015 as a nonprofit and departed its board in 2018. He subsequently filed a lawsuit against OpenAI and Sam Altman alleging the organization abandoned its open-source, nonprofit founding mission. The lawsuit is ongoing. His political activities and public positions are frequently controversial. Vursyl covers his technological contributions — xAI, SpaceX, Tesla, and Starlink — which are among the most consequential in the world.

voices.name: Mark Zuckerberg
voices.bio: Leads Meta's aggressive open-source AI strategy. The Llama model series has democratized access to frontier-class LLMs and reshaped the AI competitive landscape. Meta AI Research (FAIR) is one of the most productive labs in the world.
known_for: Meta AI assistant across all platforms
positions: Open-source AI is better for safety and innovation than closed models
AI will be the defining technology of the next decade
The metaverse and AI are complementary long-term bets

voices.name: Satya Nadella
voices.bio: Transformed Microsoft into an AI-first company. Bet early and big on OpenAI, integrating AI into every Microsoft product via Copilot. Azure is the infrastructure backbone for a significant portion of the world's AI workloads.
positions: Every company will be an AI company
Cloud and AI are inseparable infrastructure layers
Microsoft's mission — empowering every person on the planet — has never been more relevant

voices.name: Sebastian Raschka
voices.bio: Author of Build a Large Language Model from Scratch — the definitive hands-on guide to LLM internals. Researcher and educator making the most complex parts of modern AI legible to practitioners worldwide.
known_for: Build a Large Language Model from Scratch
Machine Learning with PyTorch and Scikit-Learn
High-signal AI research breakdowns on X
positions: Understanding model internals is essential for responsible AI development
The best way to learn AI is to build from scratch
Practical implementation beats theoretical abstraction for most developers

voices.name: Lex Fridman
voices.bio: MIT researcher and host of the Lex Fridman Podcast — one of the most-watched long-form interview series in the world. His conversations with Musk, Altman, Hinton, Karpathy, and dozens of others are required listening for anyone serious about the AI frontier.
known_for: Long-form interviews with frontier AI figures
positions: Long-form conversation is the best format for understanding complex ideas
AI and robotics will redefine what it means to be human
Technical depth and human connection are not mutually exclusive

voices.name: Kai-Fu Lee
voices.bio: Former president of Google China and VP at Microsoft, Apple, and SGI. Author of AI Superpowers. Leads Sinovation Ventures and co-founded 01.AI. The foremost voice on AI development in China and the geopolitics of AI competition.
positions: AI will create a new world order between the US and China
Routine cognitive tasks will be automated within a decade
AI will create more jobs than it destroys if managed well

voices.name: Logan Kilpatrick
voices.bio: Former head of developer relations at OpenAI, now at Google AI. One of the most accessible and practical voices on LLM tools, APIs, and developer ecosystem. Bridges the gap between frontier research and everyday builders.
positions: Developer experience determines which AI platforms win
Most AI applications will be built by non-AI-experts
The API layer is where AI value is actually created

voices.name: Jensen Huang
voices.bio: The indispensable hardware visionary. NVIDIA GPUs power virtually every frontier AI model in existence. Huang bet on GPU computing for AI a decade before the field agreed — and won. Net worth exceeds $100B. NVIDIA briefly became the world's most valuable company.
positions: Every industry will be transformed by accelerated computing
The next wave of AI is physical — robots and autonomous systems
Quantum computing and AI will intersect sooner than expected

voices.name: Bernard Marr
voices.bio: One of the world's most-read voices on technology trends. Bestselling author of 20+ books on AI, big data, and the future of business. Forbes contributor. Makes complex technology trends accessible to business leaders and general audiences globally.
positions: AI literacy is now a core business competency
Every business leader must understand quantum's coming impact
Technology adoption is always slower than predicted and then faster than expected

voices.name: Kate Crawford
voices.bio: Author of Atlas of AI — the definitive examination of AI's material costs, labor practices, and societal impacts. Senior Principal Researcher at Microsoft Research. Her work surfaces the infrastructure reality behind AI systems that most coverage ignores.
known_for: AI environmental and labor impact research
positions: AI systems are not neutral — they encode political and economic choices
The environmental cost of AI infrastructure is systematically underreported
Regulation must address AI's supply chain, not just its outputs

voices.name: Scott Galloway
voices.bio: NYU Stern professor, serial entrepreneur, and host of the Prof G Pod. One of the sharpest macro-level voices on tech companies, AI economics, and the political economy of big tech. Known for calling major tech trends early.
known_for: Prof G Pod and No Mercy No Malice
The Four book on big tech
Early Amazon, Apple, Google, Meta analysis
positions: Big tech AI concentration is an antitrust issue
AI will dramatically accelerate wealth inequality without policy intervention
The best investment in AI is education, not stocks

voices.name: Eric Topol
voices.bio: The most trusted voice in AI medicine. Cardiologist and author of Deep Medicine and The Patient Will See You Now. Champions AI as a tool to restore the human connection in healthcare — freeing physicians from administrative burden to focus on patients.
positions: AI will be the greatest tool in medical history if used to augment, not replace, physicians
The patient-physician relationship must be protected as AI scales
Medical AI must be validated with diverse patient populations

voices.name: Bob Wachter
voices.bio: Chair of Medicine at UCSF and author of The Digital Doctor and A Giant Leap. One of the most grounded voices on AI implementation in clinical settings — combining enthusiasm for AI's potential with hard-won experience deploying it in real hospitals.
known_for: The Digital Doctor and A Giant Leap books
positions: AI in medicine must be implemented carefully — speed without safety is dangerous
Clinician training on AI is as important as the technology itself
AI will transform clinical workflows within a decade

voices.name: Shiv Rao
voices.bio: Cardiologist turned founder. CEO of Abridge — the leading AI medical scribe platform reducing clinician documentation burden. Abridge is deployed at major health systems including UCSF, Duke, and others. At the front line of real-world AI healthcare deployment.
positions: Clinician burnout is a crisis that AI can directly address
Medical AI must be built with clinicians, not just for them
Trust in AI medical tools must be earned through transparency

voices.name: David Sinclair
voices.bio: Leading longevity scientist. Pioneer of NAD+ biology and epigenetic reprogramming research. Author of Lifespan. Co-Director of the Paul F. Glenn Center for Biology of Aging Research at Harvard. Believes aging is a disease — and that we are close to treating it.
positions: Aging is a disease, not an inevitability
We are within reach of extending healthy human lifespan by decades
The information content of DNA is preserved even as its expression degrades — and can be restored

voices.name: Jennifer Doudna
voices.bio: Nobel Prize winner in Chemistry 2020. Co-inventor of CRISPR-Cas9 gene editing with Emmanuelle Charpentier. Her work is the foundation of a new era of precision medicine — enabling targeted editing of DNA with unprecedented accuracy.
positions: CRISPR will transform medicine, agriculture, and our understanding of life itself
The ethical governance of gene editing is as important as the science
Basic research leads to transformative applications on timelines no one predicts

voices.name: Feng Zhang
voices.bio: Broad Institute scientist who pioneered the application of CRISPR to human cells — independently of and in parallel with Doudna. Also developed optogenetics tools. One of the most prolific and influential biotech inventors of his generation.
known_for: First CRISPR application in human cells
positions: CRISPR editing in human cells opens a new chapter in medicine
RNA targeting systems will be as important as DNA editing
Biotech and AI convergence will define the next era of medicine

voices.name: George Church
voices.bio: Genomics pioneer. Initiated the Human Genome Project. Developed key DNA sequencing technologies. Leads research into reversing aging, de-extinction of species, and radical genomic medicine. One of the most prolific inventor-scientists in modern biology.
positions: Genomic medicine will transform every branch of healthcare
De-extinction is both scientifically feasible and ecologically beneficial
Aging reversal at the cellular level is an engineering problem, not a philosophical one

voices.name: Peter Attia
voices.bio: Physician focused on the applied science of longevity. Author of Outlive. Host of The Drive podcast — one of the most substantive long-form health and medicine podcasts in the world. Brings rigorous scientific thinking to the practical question of how to live longer and better.
known_for: Zone 2 training and metabolic health framework
positions: Medicine 3.0 must shift from treating disease to preventing it decades in advance
Exercise is the most powerful longevity intervention available today
Metabolic health is the foundation of long-term wellbeing

voices.name: Bryan Johnson
voices.bio: Sold Braintree/Venmo to PayPal for $800M. Founded Kernel (brain-computer interface) and OS Fund. Now leads Blueprint — a self-experimentation longevity protocol tracking 111 biomarkers with the goal of achieving the body of an 18-year-old. The most public human longevity experiment in history.
positions: Don't die — the most important goal any individual can pursue
Algorithmic decision-making for personal health outperforms human intuition
The future of humanity depends on solving aging

voices.name: Nir Barzilai
voices.bio: Director of the Institute for Aging Research at Albert Einstein College of Medicine. Leading the TAME trial — the first clinical trial to target aging itself as a disease using metformin. Pioneer of the centenarian study identifying genetic factors in exceptional longevity.
known_for: FDA engagement on aging as a clinical endpoint
positions: Aging must be recognized by the FDA as a medical condition to accelerate research
Centenarians hold the genetic keys to understanding healthy aging
Metformin may be the first broadly available longevity drug

voices.name: Daniel Kraft
voices.bio: Stanford and Harvard-trained physician-scientist. Faculty chair of Medicine at Singularity University. Leading voice on the convergence of AI, robotics, genomics, and digital health. Founder of Exponential Medicine conference.
positions: Healthcare is being exponentially disrupted by converging technologies
The doctor of the future will be AI-augmented, not AI-replaced
Preventive and personalized medicine will replace reactive sick-care

voices.name: Atul Butte
voices.bio: Chief Data Scientist of the University of California Health system. Pediatrician and computational biologist. Pioneer of translational bioinformatics — mining existing biomedical data to find new drug targets and disease insights.
positions: The answers to most diseases are already in existing data — we just need to look
AI will accelerate drug discovery by orders of magnitude
Health data sharing is a moral imperative

voices.name: Brett Adcock
voices.bio: Serial entrepreneur. Founded Vettery (sold to Adecco) and Archer Aviation before founding Figure AI — building general-purpose humanoid robots for industrial applications. Figure 02 is among the most capable humanoid robots deployed in real factory environments.
positions: Humanoid robots will be the most important product category of the century
General purpose humanoids must work in the real world, not just demos
The bottleneck is software and AI, not hardware

voices.name: Marc Raibert
voices.bio: Father of dynamic robotics. Founded Boston Dynamics in 1992 as an MIT spinoff. Atlas and Spot redefined what physical machines can do. His work on legged locomotion is the foundation of every serious bipedal and quadrupedal robot program in the world.
positions: Dynamic balance is the key insight missing from early robotics
Robots must move naturally to work safely alongside humans
The gap between robot demos and real deployment is closing rapidly

voices.name: Peter Beck
voices.bio: Founder and CEO of Rocket Lab — the second most active orbital launch provider in the world after SpaceX. Built Electron, the leading small-satellite launcher, and is developing Neutron for medium-lift missions. New Zealand's most consequential tech entrepreneur.
positions: Space access must be frequent, reliable, and affordable to unlock the space economy
Small satellites will transform Earth observation, communications, and science
New Zealand and the Southern Hemisphere offer unique launch geometry advantages

voices.name: Hartmut Neven
voices.bio: Founder and director of Google Quantum AI. Led the team that announced quantum supremacy in 2019 with the Sycamore processor. Driving Google's roadmap toward fault-tolerant quantum computing and the Willow chip generation.
positions: Quantum computing progress is doubly exponential
Fault-tolerant quantum computing is achievable within this decade
Quantum and AI will be synergistic — each accelerating the other

voices.name: Krysta Svore
voices.bio: VP of Quantum at Microsoft and the architect of Microsoft's topological qubit approach. Leads the development of Azure Quantum and Q# programming language. Pioneer of quantum software infrastructure that will run on fault-tolerant hardware.
positions: Topological qubits offer a fundamentally more stable path to fault-tolerant quantum computing
Quantum software must be built now for hardware that is coming
Quantum will solve problems classical computers never can

voices.name: John Martinis
voices.bio: Superconducting qubit hardware pioneer. Led the Google quantum hardware team through the 2019 quantum supremacy experiment. Now at UCSB advancing the fundamental physics of quantum error correction.
positions: Hardware quality is the primary bottleneck for useful quantum computing
Error correction must be solved before quantum advantage is practical
The physics of superconducting qubits is well understood — engineering is the challenge

voices.name: Jerry Chow
voices.bio: Director of Quantum Hardware System Development at IBM. Leads the hardware roadmap delivering Eagle, Heron, Flamingo, and beyond. IBM Quantum has the most open-access quantum computing program in the world through IBM Quantum Network.
positions: Open access to quantum hardware accelerates the entire field
Quantum utility — solving real problems before full fault tolerance — is achievable now
The IBM roadmap to 100,000 qubit systems is on track

voices.name: Fred Chong
voices.bio: Seymour Goodman Professor of Computer Science at the University of Chicago. Leads the EPiQC (Enabling Practical-scale Quantum Computation) collaboration. Bridges quantum hardware and software with a systems engineering perspective.
positions: Quantum compilers and software are as important as hardware
Cross-layer optimization is essential for near-term quantum advantage
Quantum computing is a systems problem, not just a physics problem

voices.name: Alan Baratz
voices.bio: CEO of D-Wave — the longest-running commercial quantum computing company. D-Wave's annealing-based quantum systems are deployed in real enterprise optimization problems today. Leads the hybrid quantum-classical computing approach for near-term advantage.
positions: Quantum advantage for optimization problems is available today, not years away
Hybrid quantum-classical systems are the practical path for near-term value
Commercial deployment is the best proof of quantum utility

voices.name: Michio Kaku
voices.bio: City College of New York theoretical physicist and one of the world's most recognized science communicators. Author of Physics of the Future, The Future of the Mind, Quantum Supremacy, and many others. Makes the frontier of physics and technology legible to billions.
known_for: Physics of the Future, Quantum Supremacy books
positions: Quantum computing will be as transformative as the discovery of fire
The internet of the future will be a quantum internet
Consciousness may ultimately be explained by quantum mechanics

voices.name: Peter Diamandis
voices.bio: Founder of XPRIZE Foundation and co-founder of Singularity University. Author of Abundance and The Future Is Faster Than You Think. Radical abundance optimist. Leads Fountain Life longevity health platform. Epitomizes the pro-technology, positive-future worldview.
positions: The world's biggest problems are the world's biggest business opportunities
Exponential technologies will solve scarcity within decades
The next ten years will bring more change than the last hundred
